title: autotune: defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Desai
release_notes:
- Add autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token cost
- Introduce quantization profile selection helpers and new quant profiles for T4/A100 latency tiers
- Add unit-economics CLI and a lightweight dashboard data export to estimate token-level costs, simulate batching effects, and preview expected latency/cost tradeoffs for proposed config changes
description: Motivation: Customers repeatedly ask for sensible out-of-the-box defaults that reduce inference unit cost without manual tuning. This PR implements an autotune path that sets batching and caching defaults based on observed request distributions, exposes quantization profile recommendations for common hardware/seqlen combinations, and ships a unit-economics tooling surface to estimate per-request cost impact and provide actionable recommendations. The description below lists the user-visible changes, implementation notes, test plan, and rollout steps. User-visible changes: 1) runtime will apply configurable autodetected defaults for batch_size_targets and prefix/KV cache TTL when a route is first created (opt-out via route config). 2) New quantization profiles are introduced (q8_t4_lowlatency, q4a100_throughput) and a ProfileSelector will pick recommended profiles based on model family, hardware class, and p95 latency budget. 3) Added redwood-econ CLI subcommand and a lightweight dashboard data export to estimate token-level costs, simulate batching effects, and preview expected latency/cost tradeoffs for proposed config changes. Implementation notes: - runtime/autotune: new controller reads recent request histograms (windowed), computes heuristics for batching target and cache TTL, and writes defaults to route metadata. - runtime/quant: profile registry + selection logic with unit tests and small perf harness. - tooling/uecon: CLI to evaluate historical traces (compatible with existing observability export format) and generate recommendations (batching, cache TTL, quant profile). - docs: quickstart and migration guide for operators. Testing: unit tests added for selector heuristics, integration tests for route creation/upsert path, perf canary runs on a small set of models (gpt-small family and internal LLM-A) to validate latency and cost expectations. Rollout plan: merge to main behind a feature flag AUTOTUNE_V1, gradually enable for 10% of new routes, monitor latency SLOs and unit-cost metrics for 2 weeks, then increase to 50% if no regressions. Related: ENG-4621 (autotune heuristics), ENG-4728 (uecon tooling).

Lena Morales: The quant profiles look good; please include expected percent-cost-savings per profile in docs.
Priya Desai: Added a table in docs/uecon-howto.md with measured p50/p95 latency and cost delta from the perf canary runs.
Kai Nguyen: Integration tests flaked initially on the route upsert path (race on metadata); recommend adding a stronger retry/backoff.
Priya Desai: Added backoff + test fixture update. Re-ran integration tests.
Lena Morales: Approving after test fixes and perf canary validated for the small model set.
merge_notes: Merged to main via squash after approvals. AUTOTUNE_V1 gated by feature flag; operators must opt-in via env or route config to enable. Post-merge: ops will enable 10% rollout and monitor uecon metrics for regressions.
